newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end lower after SMI hits new high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end lower after SMI hits new high.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares closed lower on profit-taking after hitting new highs earlier in the session.

Selling in major pharmaceuticals Roche, Ciba and Sandoz as well as Nestle weighed on the market, dealers said. Wall Street shares lost steam after a strong beginning which also pressured Swiss indices, a trader said.
* The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) slipped 9.3 points, or 0.24 percent, to 3,883.3 points. The index hit a new all-time high of 3,904.6 points in early trade.
* The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended down 4.86 points, or 0.2 percent, at 2,481.69 points.

* Actively-traded Roche certificates, which had overcome the level of 10,000 francs on Tuesday to close at 10,065, rose to 10,100 early in the day but then dipped back to finish at 10,020. New warrants and recommendations had helped the stock in the beginning, but profit taking wiped out the gains, one dealer said.
* Ciba and Sandoz lost 0.3 and 0.4 percent, respectively.
* Nestle, whose 10 month sales rise of 5.7 percent was somewhat below market expectations, ended down 12 francs at 1,415. A dealer said the market had expected sales growth of 6.1 to 7.0 percent.
* Among financials, UBS jumped 17 francs, or 1.35 percent, to 1,274. One dealer said this may be due to Tuesday's weak bias and speculative buying ahead of a Nov 26 press conference.
* Swiss Re fell three francs to 1,421. Insurers Zurich and Baloise lost more than one percent after recent gains. Winterthur was up six francs to 793, possibly due to a new warrant, dealers said.
* Newcomer SEZ, holding comapany for an Austrian supplier for the microchip industry, jumped to 1,560 from 960 francs.
* Sulzer added four francs to 764 after the company said it planned to cut up to 120 jobs at its locomotive unit SLM Schweizerische Lokomotiv- und Maschinenfabrik in 1997.

* Soffex saw active trade in options on UBS, CS Holding and Winterthur Insurance while other trade was quiet. Even derivative trade in Nestle failed to react to the 10 month interim report released earlier.
* Dealers said implicit volatilities showed a wide spread reaching from low values of around 13 percent for Nestle, ABB and Holderbank to high 20 percent for some banks and insurers.
* Bank Leu's volatility index rose by 43 basis points to 16.86 percent.
* 24,344 option contracts on the SMI index changed hands with a call-put-ratio at 1:1.54.
Index futures traded with a discount at the end after a premium early in the business.
* December SMI closed 15.5 points lower at 3,882.0 after testing support at 3,875.
